doc: VALUE-BINDING radar for the session OPEN verifiers (push mode). verifyOpenTx
binds openPayload.signature to the transaction's own fee-payer signature and
(under an RPC) confirms it landed — that half of the binding is real. What is
NOT bound is the on-chain DISTRIBUTION committed in the open instruction's
recipients array: verifyOpenTx checks payee == expected.recipient (one
account) but never checks the open's recipients[] (bps -> recipient split)
against the merchant's configured splits / a challenge distributionHash. A
client can therefore open a channel whose deposit and payee look correct but
whose committed distribution routes settlement to attacker-controlled
recipients — the HIGH push-open fabricated-distribution finding. The C1 case
below is the placeholder-open bypass: an empty/placeholder signature with an
RPC configured must be rejected fleet-wide.

cases.description: C1 fabricated-deposit bypass: in client-submit mode, with an RPC configured, an empty/placeholder open signature carries no proof the deposit landed. It must be rejected. Confirmed FIXED in TS src (verifyOpenTx C1 guard); the vector keeps the fleet honest for Go/Python and guards against regression.
cases.pendingFix: each SDK's client-submit open verifier must reject an empty/placeholder signature when an RPC is configured.

cases.description: The open transaction is otherwise valid — correct payee account, deposit <= cap, channel PDA matches, real bound+confirmed signature — but the open instruction's recipients[] array commits 100% of settlement to an attacker address instead of the merchant's configured distribution. verifyOpenTx has no expected-distribution / distributionHash input and never parses recipients[], so it accepts. The channel then settles to the attacker.
cases.pendingFix: verifyOpenTx must gain an expected distribution (splits or a distributionHash from the challenge) and assert the open instruction's recipients[] match it; today the field does not exist so the divergence cannot be caught.

cases.description: Positive control for the open path: a different transaction's valid, confirmed signature paired with this open's bytes must be rejected by the signature-binding check (txSignature != openPayload.signature). This is the half of value-binding the open verifier DOES enforce; the vector pins it so a regression that drops the binding turns red.
cases.pendingFix: none — regression guard for the existing signature<->transaction binding.

cases.description: The open transaction is otherwise valid — deposit <= cap, correct mint, correct authorizedSigner, rentPayer == operator, a real bound+confirmed signature, internally-consistent channel PDA — but the open instruction's payee account (slot 2) is an ATTACKER address instead of the merchant's challenge recipient. verifyOpenTx pins payee == expected.recipient (TS on-chain.ts:618, Go session_onchain.go:230, Python verify_open_tx), so the divergence must be rejected before the channel ever opens; otherwise settlement would route to the attacker. This is the primary value-binding check every SDK's open verifier enforces — the vector keeps it green fleet-wide and guards against a regression that drops the payee binding.
cases.pendingFix: none — regression guard for the existing payee<->challenge-recipient binding.
